questions.question: ‘Kabuli Bagh Mosque’ of Panipat was constructed by which Mughal ruler?

__
 
• The Kabuli Bagh Mosque was constructed by Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• It was built in 1527 AD after Babur's victory over Ibrahim Lodhi at the First Battle of Panipat.
 
• The mosque is located in Panipat, Haryana, and serves as a significant historical and architectural landmark.
 
• It is named 'Kabuli Bagh' after Babur's wife Kabuli Begum, commemorating his victory.
 
• The mosque represents the early Mughal architecture style, combining Persian and Indian elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Battle of Panipat:**

 
 
• Fought on April 21, 1526, between the forces of Babur and Ibrahim Lodhi.
 
• Marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• Babur's use of field artillery was a decisive factor in his victory.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture:**
 
 
• Known for its large-scale use of marble, intricate carvings, and garden layouts.
 
• Famous structures include the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and Humayun's Tomb.
 
 
 
• **Babur:**
 
 
• Full name: Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur.
 
• Descendant of Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side.
 
• Authored his autobiography, Baburnama, which provides a detailed account of his life.
 
 
 
• **Panipat:**

questions.question: Right to Education has been given in which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 21A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 21A** of the Indian Constitution mandates the provision of free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• This Article was inserted by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**.
 
• The Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009 operationalizes the provisions of Article 21A.
 
• The RTE Act came into effect on **April 1, 2010**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**

 
 
• This amendment also added Article 45 and Article 51A(k) to the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 45 directs the state to provide early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years.
 
• Article 51A(k) mandates parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009**
 
 
• The RTE Act aims at providing primary education to all children in the age group of 6-14 years.
 
• It mandates 25% reservation for disadvantaged sections of the society where disadvantaged groups include SCs, STs, socially and educationally backward classes and differently-abled children.
 
• The Act requires all private schools to reserve 25% of their seats for children from these disadvantaged groups.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• These are a set of rights that are recognized by the Supreme Court as requiring a high degree of protection from government encroachment.
 
• They are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Rights are considered essential for the overall development of individuals and the nation.

questions.question: Which of the following regarding the trophic levels is INCORRECT?

• Omnivores are organisms that consume both plants and animals as their primary food sources.
 
• Fungi are not classified as omnivores; they are primarily decomposers that break down organic matter.
 
• Decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria, play a crucial role in nutrient cycling by breaking down dead organisms.
 
• Herbivores, also known as primary consumers, feed exclusively on plant material.
 
• Carnivores, which can be secondary or tertiary consumers, feed on other animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels:**

 
 
• The position an organism occupies in a food chain, which includes primary producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, and decomposers.
 
• Primary producers, like plants, convert solar energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Food Chain:**
 
 
• A linear sequence of organisms where each is fed upon by the next member in the chain.
 
 
 
• **Food Web:**
 
 
• A complex network of interconnected food chains in an ecosystem, demonstrating how different organisms are interdependent.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers:**
 
 
• Organisms like bacteria and fungi that break down dead matter, returning essential nutrients to the ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transfer:**
 
 
• In ecosystems, energy flows from primary producers through various consumer levels, with significant energy loss at each trophic level due to metabolic processes.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest density?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Solid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Solids have the highest density compared to liquids, gases, and plasma because their particles are packed closely together in a fixed structure.
 
• The density of a material is defined as its mass per unit volume. Solids generally exhibit the highest mass per unit volume among the states of matter.
 
• Examples of high-density solids include metals such as iron, gold, and lead, which have densities significantly higher than liquids and gases.
 
• Solids retain a fixed shape and volume, contributing to their higher density, whereas liquids and gases conform to the shape of their containers and have lower densities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Density**

 
 
• Density is a measure of how much mass is contained in a given unit volume of a substance.
 
• The formula for density is: Density = Mass / Volume.
 
 
 
• **States of Matter**
 
 
• There are four fundamental states of matter: solid, liquid, gas, and plasma.
 
• Each state has distinct physical properties, such as shape, volume, and particle arrangement.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Densities**
 
 
• Solids typically have the highest densities, followed by liquids, gases, and then plasma.
 
• Water has a density of approximately 1 g/cm³ at standard temperature and pressure, while air has a density of about 0.0012 g/cm³.
 
 
 
• **Plasma**
 
 
• Plasma is a high-energy state of matter where electrons are stripped from atoms, creating a mixture of positively charged ions and free electrons.
 
• Plasma densities are typically lower than those of solids, liquids, and gases under terrestrial conditions.

questions.question: Which of the below mentioned elements occurs when the government's revenue expenditure is more than its revenue receipts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Revenue Deficit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue Deficit** occurs when the government's revenue expenditure exceeds its revenue receipts.
 
• It indicates the government is not earning sufficient revenue to cover its routine expenses.
 
• Revenue Deficit needs to be managed to avoid excessive borrowing for recurring expenditures.
 
• It is a critical indicator of the financial health of the government and reflects the sustainability of its fiscal policy.
 
• High revenue deficits over time can lead to higher debt levels and interest payments, affecting the overall economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Deficit:**

 
 
• It measures the total borrowing requirements of the government.
 
• Fiscal Deficit is the difference between total expenditure and total revenue (excluding borrowings).
 
• A high fiscal deficit can lead to inflation and higher interest rates in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Budgetary Deficit:**
 
 
• It is a broad term that encompasses both revenue deficit and fiscal deficit.
 
• Budgetary Deficit indicates the overall shortfall in the government's budget.
 
 
 
• **Capital Deficit:**
 
 
• It refers to the shortfall in the capital receipts compared to the capital expenditures.
 
• Capital Deficit typically deals with long-term investments and infrastructure spending.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Receipts:**
 
 
• These are the funds received by the government from various sources like taxes, duties, and fees.
 
• Revenue Receipts do not create any liabilities or reduce any assets of the government.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Expenditure:**
 
 
• It includes all expenses incurred for the normal functioning of government departments and various services.
 
• Revenue Expenditure does not result in the creation of assets or reduction of liabilities.

questions.question: Choose the INCORRECT statement about lichens.

options.text: Lichens are seen slow-growing large coloured patches on the bark of trees.
Fungi are found in lichen living a symbiotic life.
Fungi and cyanobacteria both lives in lichens independently.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lichens are a symbiotic association between fungi and a photosynthetic partner, typically algae or cyanobacteria.
 
• The fungal component, known as the mycobiont, provides structure and protection while the photosynthetic partner, known as the photobiont, produces food through photosynthesis.
 
• Fungi and cyanobacteria do not live independently within lichens; they form a mutualistic relationship where both partners benefit.
 
• Lichens grow slowly and can form large, colored patches on surfaces like tree bark, rocks, and soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Symbiosis**

 
 
• Symbiosis is an interaction between two different organisms living in close physical association, typically to the advantage of both.
 
• In lichens, the symbiotic relationship is between a fungus and an alga or cyanobacterium.
 
 
 
• **Types of Lichens**
 
 
• Crustose: Crust-like lichens that adhere tightly to the substrate.
 
• Foliose: Leafy lichens that have a flat, leaf-like structure.
 
• Fruticose: Shrubby or hair-like lichens with a complex, branching structure.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance**
 
 
• Lichens play a vital role in soil formation by breaking down rocks into soil particles.
 
• They are bioindicators of air quality, as they are sensitive to air pollution and environmental changes.
 
 
 
• **Lichen Reproduction**
 
 
• Lichens can reproduce asexually through fragmentation, where pieces of the lichen break off and grow into new individuals.
 
• They can also reproduce sexually via fungal spores, which must encounter a compatible photosynthetic partner to form a new lichen.

questions.question: Warm days and cold nights is characteristic of which season in Northern India?

__
 
• Northern India experiences **warm days and cold nights during the summer season** due to the region's geographical and climatic conditions.
 
• The temperature difference between day and night is **significant in summer** due to clear skies and dry air.
 
• In summer, the **sun's intensity** leads to high daytime temperatures, but the heat dissipates quickly at night.
 
• The phenomenon is particularly noticeable in **desert regions** like Rajasthan, where the diurnal temperature variation is extreme.
 
• This pattern is a result of the **continental climate** experienced in Northern India, which lacks the moderating influence of large water bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diurnal Temperature Variation**

 
 
• It refers to the difference in temperature between the highest temperature during the day and the lowest temperature at night.
 
• This variation is more pronounced in arid and semi-arid regions.
 
 
 
• **Continental Climate**
 
 
• Characterized by significant seasonal temperature differences, with hot summers and cold winters.
 
• Influenced by the lack of nearby large water bodies which would otherwise moderate the temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Influence**
 
 
• Northern India’s topography, including the presence of the Thar Desert, contributes to the extreme temperature variations.
 
• The Himalayas also play a role in shaping the climate by blocking cold winds from Central Asia.
 
 
 
• **Summer Season in India**
 
 
• Typically lasts from March to June, with peak temperatures in May and June.
 
• Characterized by high temperatures during the day, often exceeding 40°C (104°F) in many areas.

questions.question: Who introduced the term 'triads' in the classification of elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Johann Dobereiner**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Johann Dobereiner, a German chemist, introduced the concept of 'triads' in 1817.
 
• He observed that certain groups of three elements (triads) had similar chemical properties and that the atomic weight of the middle element was approximately the average of the other two.
 
• Dobereiner's Triads were an early attempt to classify elements based on their properties and paved the way for the development of the periodic table.
 
• Examples of Dobereiner's Triads include lithium, sodium, and potassium, as well as calcium, strontium, and barium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table Development:**

 
 
• The periodic table as we know it today was developed by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869.
 
• Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic weight and left gaps for elements that were yet to be discovered.
 
 
 
• **Law of Triads:**
 
 
• The Law of Triads states that the arithmetic mean of the atomic weights of the first and third elements in a triad is approximately equal to the atomic weight of the second element.
 
 
 
• **Other Early Classifications:**
 
 
• John Newlands proposed the Law of Octaves, which stated that every eighth element had similar properties.
 
• A.E.B. de Chancourtois introduced the telluric helix, a three-dimensional arrangement of the elements.
 
 
 
• **Modern Periodic Law:**
 
 
• The modern periodic law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers, not atomic weights.
 
• This law was proposed by Henry Moseley in 1913 after he discovered the concept of atomic number.

questions.question: Identify a structure found in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae.

• They break down waste materials and cellular debris.

• **Erythropoiesis:**
 
 
• The process of red blood cell production.
 
• Occurs in the bone marrow.
 
• Stimulated by the hormone erythropoietin, which is produced by the kidneys in response to low oxygen levels.
 
 
 
• **Anemia:**
 
 
• A condition in which there is a deficiency of red blood cells or hemoglobin in the blood.
 
• Leads to symptoms like fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath.

• **Blood Groups:**

• **Electronic Configuration**

• The configuration follows the Aufbau principle, Hund's rule, and the Pauli exclusion principle.
 
• For example, the electronic configuration of Lithium is 1s² 2s¹.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal Deficit**__.

__
 
• Fiscal deficit is the difference between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue excluding borrowings.
 
• This deficit indicates the total amount of borrowing required by the government to meet its expenditure.
 
• It is a crucial indicator of a government's financial health and its reliance on borrowing to fund its activities.
 
• Fiscal deficit is usually expressed as a percentage of a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• Monitoring the fiscal deficit helps in understanding the sustainability of a government's policies and its financial discipline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Deficit**

 
 
• Primary deficit is the fiscal deficit of a government excluding interest payments on past borrowings.
 
• It indicates the current fiscal condition and the borrowing needed to meet current expenses.
 
• Primary deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments.
 
 
 
• **Balance of Payments (BoP) Deficit**
 
 
• BoP deficit occurs when a country's total imports of goods, services, and transfers exceed its total exports.
 
• It reflects the economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Deficit**
 
 
• Revenue deficit is the excess of the government's revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
 
• It indicates that the government is not able to meet its current operational expenses from its revenue earnings.
 
 
 
• **Implications of High Fiscal Deficit**
 
 
• A high fiscal deficit may lead to higher borrowing costs and increased public debt.
 
• It can also result in inflationary pressures if financed by printing more money.

__
 
• **Frogs have a three-chambered heart**, consisting of two atria and one ventricle.
 
• The three-chambered heart in amphibians like frogs allows for partial mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
• This structure is efficient for their dual life in water and on land, where they can absorb oxygen through their skin.
 
• Unlike frogs, birds and mammals possess a more complex four-chambered heart, which completely separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heart Chambers in Vertebrates**

 
 
• **Fish:** Two-chambered heart (one atrium and one ventricle)
 
• **Amphibians:** Three-chambered heart (two atria and one ventricle)
 
• **Reptiles:** Typically three-chambered heart, except for crocodiles which have four chambers
 
• **Birds and Mammals:** Four-chambered heart (two atria and two ventricles)
 
 
 
• **Functions of Heart Chambers**
 
 
• Atria receive blood from the body and lungs.
 
• Ventricles pump blood out to the body and lungs.
 
• A four-chambered heart allows for complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, which is more efficient for high-energy demands.
 
 
 
• **Circulatory Systems**
 
 
• **Single Circulatory System:** Found in fish, blood passes through the heart once during each complete circuit.
 
• **Double Circulatory System:** Found in amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals, blood passes through the heart twice, providing more efficient oxygenation.
 
 
 
• **Adaptive Significance**
 
 
• A four-chambered heart supports endothermy (warm-bloodedness) in birds and mammals.
 
• Efficient circulation is crucial for sustaining high metabolic rates and activity levels.

• **Redshift**
 
 
• Redshift refers to the phenomenon where the light from an object is shifted to longer wavelengths as it moves away from the observer.
 
• Hubble used redshift measurements to determine the velocities of galaxies.
 
 
 
• **Big Bang Theory**

• Hubble's discovery of the expanding universe provided significant support for this theory.
